design.r_convention: sweep.retained on ser[:K] (median channel of the renormalised head output) vs the exact continuation sweep_period.tone(1, b, [phi]) at the true fractional b: r = ||P_b yhat||^2 / ||P_b y||^2, dk = khat - 1
design.grad_E: grad_h of E_b(h) = ||P_b ser(h)||^2 / o (head_direction.grad_E), ser = median channel of the raw head output
design.p_aligned: <h, grad E_b>^2 with grad E_b at the phase-matched working reference: h(4.8) for b < 5.7, h(5.8) for b >= 5.7; unnormalised gradient
design.p_aligned_p0: same but with the phi=0 references (robustness variant)
design.p_max_span: grad E_b' for b' in {4, 4.58, 5, 5.33, 6, 8}; 'own' reference convention of head_direction: at h(b') except the nulls b' in {5, 6} which use h(4.8)
design.cos_null: n_hat = first principal direction (SVD) of the mean-subtracted {h(5.0, phi), h(6.0, phi)} over the six phases; sign fixed so n_hat . (mean null state) > 0, i.e. larger cos_null = deeper into the null (the pre-registered P3 polarity)
design.cos_null_carrier: diagnostic added to the spec set: first PC of the UNCENTRED null states (dominant common null direction, well defined), cosine of h with it
design.p_local: diagnostic added to the spec set: <h, grad E_b(h)>^2, the local linearisation at the cell's own state (a degree-2 homogeneous head would give p_local = 4 E_b(h)^2, hence r proportional to it)
design.cos2_align: (h . g_own)^2 / (||h||^2 ||g_own||^2); extra diagnostic (the alignment with the reference gradient, scale-free)
design.scaling: features are reported in raw units (no standardisation); the held-out models are ordinary least squares with an intercept
design.split: primary: np.random.default_rng(0) permutation, first half train, second half test; robustness over 50 random halves and leave-one-phase-out (out-of-fold over all cells)
design.revin_note: for unit-power tones the last-patch running stats are mu=0, sigma=1, so ser equals the raw median head channel (checked: max|diff| = 5.03e-03)

null_pca.degeneracy_note: the mean-subtracted null set is two phase rings of very different radius (mean norms 61 vs 114), so PC1 mixes the phase and the radius difference and is only weakly separated (PC1/PC2 = 1.35, shares 0.465/0.255); the uncentred carrier direction is the well-defined alternative

P3_cos_null_predicts_floor_and_dk.note: judged against the five spec'd features; the added diagnostic cos_null_carrier is the well-defined null direction and beats it slightly, and p_local dominates both

reading.one_line: p_aligned (Spearman +0.462 with r) gives held-out R^2 0.104 on the seeded half and 0.112 leave-one-phase-out; the 2-feature model (p_aligned, cos_null) gives 0.532.  Best |rho| feature for r is p_local, for dk is p_local; the best held-out r model is 'M4: p_local' at 0.726.
